## 2. Technical Specializations & Engineering Architecture

### 2.1 Autonomous Agent Systems & AI Architecture
- **Agentic Workflows**: Design and implementation of multi-step reasoning loops (ReAct, Plan-and-Solve, Self-Refine) capable of executing tasks autonomously.
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: Custom MCP server implementations connecting frontier reasoning models (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT) with local filesystems, operating system commands, databases, and custom APIs.
- **Browser Automation via LLMs**: Visual and DOM-based browser agents that navigate complex SPAs, bypass dynamic hurdles, interact with form fields, and harvest structured intelligence.
- **Frameworks & Libraries**: LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Browser-Use, Playwright, Selenium, AsyncIO.

### 2.2 Generative AI (GenAI) & Production RAG Pipelines
- **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)**: Enterprise-grade document intelligence pipelines utilizing hybrid search strategies (dense semantic embeddings combined with BM25 sparse keyword search) and cross-encoder reranking.
- **LPU & Inference Optimization**: Sub-second token delivery utilizing Groq LPU hardware acceleration and lightweight embedding models.
- **Vector Databases & Storage**: Experience with FAISS, ChromaDB, pgvector, and memory-mapped persistent indices.
- **Domain Specialization**: Deep experience in legal text processing, automated statutory citation mapping, text-to-SQL synthesis, and context-aware business communication.

### 2.3 Flutter & High-Framerate Mobile Systems
- **Cross-Platform Engineering**: Production mobile engineering across iOS and Android with 60fps/120fps fluid UI pipelines.
- **Dart C++ FFI (Foreign Function Interface)**: Direct binding to low-level native C/C++ libraries for computational tasks, cryptographic processing, and hardware interactions without platform channel overhead.
- **Offline-First Data Architecture**: Resilient local-first architectures with SQLite, Hive, reactive event caching, and background sync reconciliation.
- **State Management**: Scalable state architectures with BLoC pattern, Provider, and Riverpod.

### 2.4 Systems Engineering, Computer Vision & Security
- **Backend & APIs**: High-throughput asynchronous RESTful and WebSocket microservices built on FastAPI, Flask, and Node.js.
- **Computer Vision**: Real-time edge and cloud video analytics using OpenCV, motion detection heuristics, background subtraction, and Haar cascade classifiers.
- **Algorithmic Security & Cryptography**: Custom cryptographic pipelines, steganographic unicode ciphers, and secure key lifecycle management.

## 3. Comprehensive Open-Source Projects Directory

The portfolio includes browser-local interactive illustrations for all projects. Sample outputs are distinct from real project results.

### AI Browser Automation

Turn a plain-language task into browser actions, from filling forms to collecting information.

- Intended audience: People repeating the same tasks across websites.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/AI-Agent-Browser-Automation
- Implementation: Python and Gradio provide the WebUI; browser-use and Playwright connect the agent to the browser. The repository credits the browser-use foundation.

### Indian Law AI Assistant

Make legal documents easier to understand with plain-language explanations and Indian-language translations.

- Intended audience: Readers who need help understanding a legal document.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/Indian-Law-AI-Assistant
- Implementation: The Python app supports OpenAI and Google Gemini models. The sample uses fictional excerpts and prepared translations; it provides no legal advice.

### QueryAI

Ask a business question in ordinary language and explore the answer as a table or chart.

- Intended audience: Business teams exploring information held in a database.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/QueryAI.An-AI-powered-Data-Query-Interface
- Implementation: The README describes React, Gemini, database APIs, and D3.js / Chart.js. This portfolio sample uses fixed questions and fictional sales data.

### SingleTap

Explore how a Flutter interface can pass a task to native code and bring the result back to the screen.

- Intended audience: Teams exploring Flutter applications with native processing.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/SingleTap
- Implementation: This illustrates the Flutter / Dart FFI / C++ approach described in the portfolio. Repository documentation was unavailable during verification; no performance claims are made.

### HealthOS

Bring patient, doctor, hospital, and lab workflows together in a shared Flutter health platform.

- Intended audience: Patients and care teams working across appointments and reports.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/healthos
- Implementation: Flutter with Riverpod and GoRouter forms the frontend. Supabase provides the backend; Gemini is accessed via Edge Functions. The timeline sample shows fictional records, without diagnosis.

### Expenses Tracker

Keep everyday spending in one place and see how individual expenses add up.

- Intended audience: People who want a clearer view of their spending.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/expenses-tracker_app
- Implementation: The repository description confirms Flutter, Firebase, and BLoC. Budget calculations here are portfolio sample behavior, without claims about production features.

### MCP Code Analysis

Give coding agents structured context about a Python project: its files, functions, and potential issues.

- Intended audience: Developers and agent builders exploring Python codebases.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/MCP-Server
- Implementation: The repository uses the Python standard library. Its README lists full JSON-RPC MCP server registration as roadmap work. The sample illustrates tool requests rather than a connected MCP session.

### GenAI Email Writer

Connect a job listing to relevant portfolio work and turn that context into a personalized outreach email.

- Intended audience: People preparing targeted professional outreach.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/GenAi-Email-Writter
- Implementation: The documented stack uses Streamlit, LangChain, and Groq. Sample jobs, tone choices, and drafts are prepared locally; no email is sent.

### Family Tree

Build a family tree and make the connections between relatives easier to discover.

- Intended audience: Families documenting people and their relationships.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/family-tree
- Implementation: The Plink Tree README describes Flutter, flutter_bloc, GoRouter, and Firebase. The sample contains fictional people and expandable branches.

### HomeBuildAI

Explore a rule-based approach to home design and how sample planning assumptions affect material costs.

- Intended audience: People exploring an early home-design idea.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/HomeBuildAI
- Implementation: The README identifies a rule-based home design generator in Flutter. The material calculator is an educational illustration with explicit coefficients, excluding labour and other construction costs.

### AI Stock Trading

Bring market data and news sentiment into a trading dashboard and decision pipeline.

- Intended audience: Developers exploring market-data and sentiment workflows.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/AI-Stock-Trading-APP
- Implementation: The README describes FastAPI, stock APIs, brokerage integrations, and Flutter. The local replay uses fictitious prices and illustrative risk rules; it places no trades and makes no return claims.

### Mobile Sales Analysis

Explore mobile-phone listings to understand how brands, prices, and customer ratings compare.

- Intended audience: Analysts examining a mobile marketplace dataset.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/Mobile_Sales_Analysis
- Implementation: The README describes Pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn. The portfolio uses a separate fictional monthly sales fixture so visitors can try filters.

### News Summarization

Explore company news, compare sentiment, and turn article information into a shorter briefing.

- Intended audience: Readers following news about a company.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/News-Summarization
- Implementation: The repository documents Streamlit, FastAPI, TextBlob, NLTK, and gTTS. The sample compares fictional articles with prepared summaries; it fetches no live news.

### Rock vs Mine Prediction

Explore a classification task that distinguishes rock and mine samples from sonar signals.

- Intended audience: Learners and developers exploring signal classification.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/Rock-vs-Mine-Prediction
- Implementation: The repository description confirms the sonar-classification objective; a README was unavailable. The sample reveals fixed labeled examples, without running a model or claiming accuracy.

### Cloud CCTV Footage

Organize camera recordings so authorized users can find and review footage through a shared system.

- Intended audience: Teams managing recordings from multiple cameras.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/cloud-based-CCTV-footage
- Implementation: The README describes storage, streaming, playback, and access control, but lists multiple possible technologies. This explorer does not claim a specific deployed cloud architecture.

### CCTV Surveillance Prototype

Explore a dashboard concept that brings camera feeds, search, and alerts into one view.

- Intended audience: Teams evaluating a camera-monitoring interface.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/cctv-surveillance-prototype
- Implementation: The repository identifies an HTML dashboard prototype. This sample uses drawn scenes and fixed overlays; it performs no facial recognition or live detection.

### Text to Emoji Encoding

Turn a message into an emoji sequence, then decode it to recover the original text.

- Intended audience: People exploring a playful way to represent text.
- Repository: https://github.com/kiranimmadi2/Text-to-Emoji-Encryption-and-Decryption
- Implementation: This sample maps UTF-8 bytes to pairs of emoji symbols so Unicode text can round-trip. It is a portfolio implementation of the encoding idea, not an AES cipher.
